# OVHcloud TypeScript SDK

> The TypeScript client for the OVHcloud API (github.com/ovh/sdk-typescript): 80
> API sections and 6180 operations, as typed methods on one client. OAuth2
> service-account authentication, typed errors, async iterators over lists, helpers that wait
> for asynchronous work, and a read-only mode to explore an account safely. No runtime
> dependency: it runs on Node.js, Deno and Bun. Most of the code is generated from the API's
> OpenAPI specifications.

Before you write a call, look up the method of its route in the operation index: guessing
names from the URL is not reliable. The index also gives the IAM actions of each method: the
ones the program calls are what its service account needs. The types of a section are in
dist/api/<section>/models.d.ts of the installed package: grep `export interface X ` there.

This is not node-ovh (`npm install ovh`, `require("ovh")`, `requestPromised`). Here:
`import { Client } from "@ovhcloud/sdk"`, an OAuth2 service account instead of application
keys and consumer keys, and a typed method for each API call: node-ovh's
`requestPromised("GET", "/me")` is `client.me.getAccountDetails()`.

## Docs

- [Guide](README.md): install and run on Node.js, Deno, Bun and edge workers, first program, coming from node-ovh, finding an operation and its types, arguments, updating an object, pagination, waiting for asynchronous work, errors, configuration, raw calls, testing, observability, troubleshooting
- [Examples](examples/README.md): small programs to run or copy: your account, list with an iterator, create then wait, a DNS record, a cart order, a raw call with `path()`, error handling, vRack
- [Agent notes](AGENTS.md): the conventions in short, for AI coding agents
- [Operation index](index/README.md): one index/<section>.jsonl per section, 6962 methods in all, each line a method with its route, TypeScript signature and IAM actions

- [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md): what changed in each release
